name: Hospitality & Event Management
notes: Official FBLA 2025-26 Hospitality and Event Management guideline PDF could not be retrieved (fbla.org returned 403; the NYS 2025-26 guidelines URL returned 404; no PAFBLA copy for this event was found). Competency areas are standard high-school hospitality and event-management curriculum areas, cross-checked against Idaho CTE Hospitality Management program standards (Performance Standard 6.2 Events, and related food, lodging and guest service standards). Re-check against the official event guideline when available. Questions are scenario-led for a case study event and use U.S. conventions (GAAP for nonprofit donations, FLSA overtime, ADA access, U.S. fire-code occupancy).

questions.q: A chapter has eight weeks to plan a 300-guest awards banquet. Which task should the event coordinator complete first?
choices: Define the event goals, guest count and budget, then confirm the date
Order centerpieces for each table
Hire a DJ for the reception
Print the event programs
questions.explain: Goals, audience size and budget drive every later decision, including venue size, catering and vendor choices, so they come before any purchase.

questions.q: Which planning tool shows the sequence of dependent tasks and identifies the longest chain of tasks that sets the minimum time needed to finish the project?
choices: A Gantt chart with no dependency lines
A critical path method (CPM) network diagram
A SWOT analysis
A guest satisfaction survey
questions.explain: CPM links dependent tasks; any delay on the critical path delays the whole event, which is why it is tracked closely.

questions.q: A run-of-show document is best described as:
choices: A list of vendor contract terms
A budget variance report
A minute-by-minute timeline of every activity, speaker, cue and staff assignment on event day
A guest registration form
questions.explain: The run-of-show is the operational script the team uses during the event itself.

questions.q: A planner learns that an outdoor reception has a 40 percent chance of rain. What is the most effective step?
choices: Ignore the forecast until the morning of the event
Cancel the event as soon as any rain is forecast
Buy umbrellas for all guests in advance
Reserve an indoor backup space and set a decision date for choosing between the two sites
questions.explain: A contingency plan with a backup space and a decision deadline protects the event without cancelling early on a forecast alone.

questions.q: Which objective is written as a SMART objective?
choices: Recruit 40 volunteers and raise $1,500 for the food bank by March 15
Make the banquet fun
Try to get more people involved this year
Improve the chapter's reputation
questions.explain: SMART objectives are specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound; only one choice has a number and a deadline.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a floor plan in event planning?
choices: To list vendor invoices
To show seating, stage, service and exit locations so the layout can be checked for flow and fire-code compliance
To record guest dietary needs
To track ticket sales
questions.explain: A scaled floor plan lets the planner check aisle widths, exits and service routes before the event.

questions.q: A three-day conference expects a breakout room to exceed its capacity on day two. Which action best solves the problem while protecting the schedule?
choices: Cancel the session
Ask attendees to share seats informally
Move the session to a larger room in the same venue and update signage and the event app
Shorten all sessions to 15 minutes
questions.explain: Relocating within the same venue and updating every channel fixes capacity without losing content or breaking the schedule.

questions.q: Which element belongs in a complete day-of event timeline?
choices: Final invoice payment dates only
Post-event survey results
Long-term brand strategy
Load-in and setup times, rehearsal, guest arrival and breakdown, with a named staff owner for each
questions.explain: A day-of timeline assigns times and owners to every phase, not just the main program.

questions.q: What does a rain date or backup date protect against?
choices: Loss of the event date due to weather or other disruption
Price increases from vendors
Guests forgetting to RSVP
Inflation in catering costs
questions.explain: A pre-set backup date keeps the event alive if the original date is disrupted.

questions.q: A planner's schedule sets the final catering headcount for day 20, but the RSVP deadline is day 25. What is the best fix?
choices: Keep the schedule, since the caterer can add guests later at no cost
Move the RSVP deadline before the catering headcount deadline, with a buffer for late requests
Remove the catering headcount step
Ask the caterer to guess the number
questions.explain: The headcount must be locked after RSVPs close; reversing the order creates an unplanned cost or waste.

questions.q: Which factor should be assessed first when selecting a venue for a 200-person conference?
choices: The color of the walls
Whether the parking lot has a coffee cart
Capacity for the planned layout, including exits and the fire-code occupancy limit
The brand of the projector
questions.explain: Capacity and legal occupancy are non-negotiable, so they screen venues before any preference is considered.

questions.q: A banquet needs seating for 200 guests at round tables of 10. How many tables are needed?
questions.explain: 200 divided by 10 is 20. Using 8 seats per table (25 tables) is a common error that wastes space.

questions.q: Which room setup is best for a lecture-style session where attendees take notes and no meals are served?
choices: Theater style
Banquet rounds
Cabaret
Hollow square
questions.explain: Theater style uses rows facing the front, which maximizes seats for a presentation without tables for dining.

questions.q: Before signing an outdoor venue contract, which question is most important to ask the site manager?
choices: Does the building have a restaurant on site?
What is the backup plan, and what are the rules on permits, noise limits and weather cancellation?
What is the price of the house wine?
Is the building painted in neutral colors?
questions.explain: Permits, noise rules and weather policy can cancel or disrupt an outdoor event, so they must be settled up front.

questions.q: Which term describes the maximum number of people a room may hold under fire-safety rules?
choices: Net revenue
Attendance quota
Occupancy load
Floor ratio
questions.explain: The occupancy load is set by the local fire authority and must not be exceeded.

questions.q: A venue charges $3,000 for room rental, $25 per guest for 150 guests, and a $500 setup fee. What is the total venue cost?
questions.explain: 3,000 plus (25 times 150 = 3,750) plus 500 equals 7,250. Forgetting the setup fee gives $6,750.

questions.q: Which layout decision best supports smooth guest flow at registration?
choices: Placing check-in tables at the main entrance with signage and extra lanes for peak arrival
Placing registration at the far end of the hall from the entrance
Using a single table with no signage
Moving check-in to the stage
questions.explain: Registration at the entrance with clear signage and extra lanes prevents bottlenecks at peak arrival times.

questions.q: A venue contract includes a minimum food and beverage spend of $4,000, but projected catering spend is $2,800. What is the best action?
choices: Ignore it, since minimums are not enforceable
Negotiate a lower minimum or add items to reach it, and confirm the final terms in writing before signing
Cancel the venue
Reduce the guest count to save money
questions.explain: Minimum spend clauses are negotiable, and the shortfall is a real cost that must be resolved before the contract is signed.

questions.q: In U.S. event planning, what does ADA compliance require of a venue layout?
choices: A dance floor in every room
Only round tables
Accessible routes, entrances and restrooms, including for wheelchair users
A stage in every room
questions.explain: The Americans with Disabilities Act requires accessible routes and facilities in public accommodations, including event venues.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a site inspection before a major event?
choices: To sign the contract for the first time
To choose the menu
To send invitations
To confirm sightlines, power, load-in access, restrooms and exits match the plan
questions.explain: A site visit verifies that the plan works in the actual space, catching problems before they become day-of failures.

questions.q: What is a budget variance?
choices: The difference between budgeted and actual amounts for a line item
The total of all guest payments
The number of vendors used
The ticket price
questions.explain: A variance measures how far actual results are from the budget, favorable or unfavorable.

questions.q: Which of these is a fixed cost for a conference?
choices: A per-plate meal charge
A venue rental fee paid regardless of attendance
A per-guest printed badge
A commission on sponsorship sales
questions.explain: Fixed costs do not change with attendance; per-guest and commission costs are variable.

questions.q: A chapter sells 120 tickets at $25 each and has $2,400 in total expenses. What is the net profit?
questions.explain: Revenue is 120 times 25, which is 3,000. Subtracting expenses of 2,400 leaves 600.

questions.q: Break-even attendance is found by dividing total fixed costs by which value?
choices: Total variable costs
Total revenue
The number of vendors
Contribution margin per guest (ticket price minus variable cost per guest)
questions.explain: Each guest contributes the ticket price less variable cost toward fixed costs; dividing gives the guests needed to cover them.

questions.q: Fixed costs are $1,800, the ticket price is $30, and variable cost is $12 per guest. What is the break-even attendance?
questions.explain: The contribution margin is 30 minus 12, which is 18. Then 1,800 divided by 18 equals 100 guests.

questions.q: What is a contingency reserve in an event budget?
choices: Money spent on the main speaker
Money set aside, usually as a percentage of the budget, for unexpected costs
Money from sponsors that is spent immediately
Profit paid out to the chapter
questions.explain: The reserve absorbs surprises such as price increases or weather costs without breaking the budget.

questions.q: A sponsor donates $1,000 of printed banners instead of cash. How should the chapter record the donation?
choices: As zero, since no cash changed hands
As a cash expense
As in-kind revenue with an equal expense at fair value when the banners are used
As a long-term liability
questions.explain: Under U.S. GAAP for nonprofits, donated goods are recorded at fair value as revenue, with an expense when used.

questions.q: Which is the best way to control spending during an event?
choices: Let each committee spend freely and reconcile at the end
Pay all vendors in cash without receipts
Skip the budget for small events
Track actual spending against each budget line daily and approve any change in writing
questions.explain: Daily tracking against budget lines catches overruns while there is still time to correct them.

questions.q: A food budget is $900 for 150 guests. The caterer quotes $8.50 per guest. What is the result?
choices: $1,275, over budget
$900, within budget
$1,050, within budget
$1,175, over budget
questions.explain: 150 times 8.50 equals 1,275, which is 375 over the $900 budget.

questions.q: Which statement about accrual and cash accounting for an event is correct?
choices: Cash basis records revenue when it is earned, regardless of payment
Accrual basis records revenue when earned and expenses when incurred, regardless of when cash moves
Accrual basis tracks only cash received
Cash basis is required by GAAP for all events
questions.explain: Accrual accounting matches income and costs to the period they relate to, which is why it is preferred for multi-period comparison.

questions.q: Which document defines the scope, price and responsibilities between an event planner and a caterer?
choices: A run-of-show
A floor plan
A signed contract or letter of agreement
An invoice
questions.explain: A signed agreement sets what is delivered, when, at what price, and who is responsible if something goes wrong.

questions.q: A vendor contract includes a force majeure clause. What does it address?
choices: Late payment penalties
Guest ticket refunds
Trademark use
Unforeseen events beyond either party's control, such as severe weather or government orders, that may excuse performance
questions.explain: Force majeure clauses allocate risk for events outside the parties' control; their scope depends on the exact wording.

questions.q: Which is the strongest reason to get three bids before hiring an audio-visual vendor?
choices: It allows comparison of price, scope, reliability and references before awarding the job
Bids are always cheaper than single quotes
It removes the need for a contract
Vendors must provide free equipment
questions.explain: Comparing scope and references matters as much as price; the cheapest bid is not always the best value.

questions.q: What is a deposit in a vendor agreement?
choices: The final payment due after the event
A partial payment that secures the date and is usually non-refundable or subject to a cancellation schedule
A penalty for late cancellation only
A tip paid to staff
questions.explain: Deposits reserve the vendor's time; the refund terms should be spelled out in the contract.

questions.q: A caterer requires a final guest count seven days before the event, and later changes are billed at 100 percent of the per-plate price. RSVPs are still changing. What is the best action?
choices: Ignore the deadline and pay later
Ask the caterer to cancel
Confirm the count with a sensible buffer and clarify the change policy in writing before the deadline
Order for 500 guests to avoid all risk
questions.explain: Locking a count with a buffer, while knowing the cost of changes, avoids paying for unused meals without risking shortages.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a certificate of insurance requested from a vendor?
choices: To prove the vendor is profitable
To register the vendor's trademark
To set the vendor's price
To confirm the vendor carries liability coverage that protects the chapter
questions.explain: A certificate shows the vendor's coverage limits and names the chapter as additional insured if the contract requires it.

questions.q: Which term describes an outside business that supplies services under a written agreement with defined deliverables?
choices: Contractor
Volunteer
Sponsor
Guest
questions.explain: A contractor delivers defined services for a fee; the contract, not the relationship, defines the obligations.

questions.q: Which statement best describes a verbal agreement for a one-day event service?
choices: Verbal agreements are never enforceable
Verbal agreements can be enforceable, but a written agreement makes the terms easier to prove
Verbal agreements are enforceable only if notarized
Verbal agreements must be filed with the state
questions.explain: Oral contracts can bind parties, but proof of terms is the problem; a written agreement avoids disputes.

questions.q: Which practice best protects a chapter when a vendor fails to deliver a rented sound system?
choices: Pay the full balance before the event
Accept any substitute without notice
Enforce the contract's delivery and remedy terms, and document the failure in writing
Cancel all other vendors
questions.explain: Written documentation and the contract's remedy clause are what support a refund or credit claim.

questions.q: A venue contract says a cancellation within 60 days costs 50 percent of the rental fee, and within 14 days costs 100 percent. The chapter cancels on day 30. What must it pay?
choices: Nothing, because it cancelled more than 14 days out
100 percent of the rental fee
25 percent of the rental fee
50 percent of the rental fee
questions.explain: Day 30 falls inside the 60-day window but outside 14 days, so the 50 percent tier applies.

questions.q: Which promotion method is most effective for a small chapter's bake sale at low cost?
choices: Social media posts, school announcements and posters in high-traffic areas
A paid television ad
A billboard on the highway
A direct mail campaign to every household
questions.explain: Free and targeted channels reach the chapter's real audience at minimal cost.

questions.q: What is a target audience?
choices: Everyone who might ever attend
The specific group the event is designed for and most likely to attend
The sponsors who pay for the event
The venue staff
questions.explain: Targeting narrows messaging, channel choice and pricing to the people most likely to say yes.

questions.q: Flyers produced 25 percent of attendees, and social media produced none. What is the most useful next step?
choices: Stop all marketing
Spend more on the same flyers
Track the source of each registration and shift budget toward the channels producing attendees
Hire a celebrity speaker
questions.explain: Source tracking shows which channels work, so spending follows results instead of habit.

questions.q: Which metric best measures the reach of a social media campaign?
choices: Number of event staff
Venue capacity
Price per plate
Impressions and unique accounts reached
questions.explain: Reach measures how many people saw the content; engagement and conversion are separate metrics.

questions.q: Which content is most effective for a promotional flyer?
choices: A clear headline with the event name, date, time, location and a call to action
A long paragraph about chapter history
A list of every vendor
A photo with no text
questions.explain: A flyer must answer the basic questions in seconds because it is read briefly.

questions.q: Last month 50 of 1,000 website visitors registered. This month 80 of 1,200 registered. Which conclusion is correct?
choices: Conversion fell from 6.7 to 5.0 percent
Conversion improved from 5.0 to 6.7 percent
Conversion was unchanged at 5 percent
Conversion cannot be compared across months
questions.explain: Conversion is registrations divided by visitors: 50/1,000 is 5.0 percent and 80/1,200 is 6.7 percent.

questions.q: Which approach best uses sponsorship benefits to attract sponsors?
choices: Offering free admission with no recognition
Hiding the sponsor's logo
Offering a defined package with measurable visibility, such as logo placement and social mentions
Charging the sponsor after the event
questions.explain: Sponsors buy defined, measurable exposure; vague promises rarely close.

questions.q: What is a call to action in promotional material?
choices: The venue's name
The sponsor's slogan
A list of event rules
A specific instruction telling the audience what to do next, such as register by a date
questions.explain: A call to action converts interest into behavior, such as registering or buying a ticket.

questions.q: What is a key benefit of early-bird ticket pricing?
choices: It encourages early commitment and gives the chapter an early head count for planning
It lowers the event's fixed costs
It removes the need for registration
It guarantees sponsorship money
questions.explain: Early sales improve planning accuracy and cash flow, though they reduce average ticket revenue.

questions.q: A chapter wants to know whether its Instagram promotion drove the event. Which pair of metrics best shows impact on the event itself?
choices: Likes and follower count
Registrations or ticket sales from tracked links, and attendance at check-in
Post length and emoji count
Impressions and comment count
questions.explain: Impressions and comments measure the post; only tracked registrations and check-ins measure the event outcome.

questions.q: Which action best improves the guest experience at check-in?
choices: Requiring guests to wait for a manual sign-up
Having one volunteer handle all tasks
Pre-printed name badges, alphabetical lanes and trained greeters
Asking guests to find their own badges
questions.explain: Pre-printed badges and split lanes shorten waits and make the first impression smooth.

questions.q: A guest with a severe food allergy is seated where the meal contains the allergen. What is the best first step?
choices: Tell the guest to eat it anyway
Ignore it, since the allergy was on the RSVP
Move the guest out of the event
Inform the kitchen and servers, and confirm the item is safe before service
questions.explain: Allergy safety is the first priority; confirming with the kitchen prevents a medical emergency.

questions.q: What does service recovery mean?
choices: Restoring a guest's trust after a service failure through an apology and corrective action
Reducing service staff to save money
Recovering lost deposits
Recording guest complaints for marketing
questions.explain: Good recovery turns a failure into a retained guest, often more loyal than before.

questions.q: Which is an example of a guest touchpoint?
choices: An accounting ledger entry
The venue's registration desk, the event app or a follow-up email
A vendor invoice
A tax form
questions.explain: A touchpoint is any moment a guest interacts with the event, which is where the experience is shaped.

questions.q: A conference survey averages 4.6 out of 5, but 30 percent of attendees skipped the food question. What is the most accurate interpretation?
choices: The event was an overall failure
Food was clearly the best element
The average is strong, but skipped questions can hide a problem, so the chapter should follow up with a targeted question
The survey is invalid and should be deleted
questions.explain: High averages can mask gaps; nonresponse on a topic is a signal worth investigating.

questions.q: A guest complains about a long line at registration. Which response is best?
choices: Tell the guest to wait without comment
Argue that the line is normal
Ask the guest to leave
Acknowledge the wait, give an updated time estimate, and open another lane or point to a shorter line
questions.explain: Acknowledging the problem and offering a concrete fix changes the guest's experience immediately.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a post-event guest feedback survey?
choices: To measure satisfaction and identify improvements for future events
To sell next year's tickets
To set vendor prices
To collect sponsor payments
questions.explain: Feedback is most useful as an input for improving the next event.

questions.q: A hotel guest reports noise from a nearby ballroom event. Which response reflects good hospitality practice?
choices: Ignore it until checkout
Offer a room change and log the issue so the event team can address the noise
Charge the guest for the inconvenience
Tell the guest it is not their concern
questions.explain: Solving the guest's problem and passing the root cause to the event team is standard hospitality practice.

questions.q: In service quality models, what is the service gap?
choices: The difference between a venue's cost and its price
The gap between two event dates
The difference between what guests expect and what they perceive they received
The difference between cash and card payments
questions.explain: Service quality is measured by the difference between expectations and perceived performance, which is why expectations must be managed.

questions.q: Which practice matters most for guests with mobility needs?
choices: Accessible seating placed in a separate area with no route
Asking guests to bring a helper
Holding the event only on an upper floor
Reserved accessible seating with step-free routes, communicated in advance
questions.explain: Accessibility requires both the seating and a usable route to it, and it should be confirmed before the event.

questions.q: What does FIFO mean in food storage?
choices: First in, first out, meaning older stock is used before newer stock
Fresh items are only ordered on Fridays
Food is inventoried only when finished
Frozen items are only sold outside
questions.explain: FIFO reduces spoilage by rotating stock so older items are used first.

questions.q: What is the food temperature danger zone?
choices: 32 to 40 degrees F
40 to 140 degrees F (about 4 to 60 degrees C)
0 to 10 degrees F
180 to 212 degrees F
questions.explain: Bacteria multiply fastest in this range, so hot and cold holding must stay outside it.

questions.q: A caterer expects 1.1 buffet plates per guest for 150 guests. How many plates should be prepared?
questions.explain: 150 times 1.1 is 165. The 10 percent buffer covers second helpings without wild over-production.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a HACCP plan?
choices: To set menu prices
To schedule staff breaks
To track guest preferences
To identify and control food hazards at critical control points to keep food safe
questions.explain: HACCP is a systematic food-safety method built around critical control points.

questions.q: What is a standard recipe used for in event catering?
choices: Consistent portions and per-guest costing
Setting the venue rental fee
Choosing the guest room layout
Assigning seating
questions.explain: A standard recipe lets the caterer predict cost and quality per guest, the basis for accurate quotes.

questions.q: A plated dinner has $18 of food cost per guest, and the target food cost percentage is 30 percent. What menu price per guest meets the target?
questions.explain: Food cost percentage is food cost divided by price, so price is 18 divided by 0.30, which is 60.

questions.q: Which beverage practice most reduces liability when alcohol is served at an event?
choices: Serving unlimited drinks to all guests
Letting guests self-serve from open bottles
Checking IDs, serving responsibly, and using a licensed bartender under an approved permit
Serving anyone who asks
questions.explain: Liability for over-service falls on the host, so licensing, ID checks and responsible service are essential.

questions.q: In banquet pricing, what is a cover?
choices: A tablecloth fee
A reservation deposit
Sales tax on food
A guest or place setting charged for a meal
questions.explain: Per-cover pricing charges by the number of guests served, not by the number of dishes.

questions.q: Which is the best way to reduce food waste after a buffet?
choices: Forecast guest counts from RSVPs and plan smaller, refilled batches
Order double the food to be safe
Throw out all leftovers without tracking
Serve only dessert
questions.explain: Good forecasting and refill planning cut waste while keeping the buffet full.

questions.q: A food truck arrives with a permit that expired two days before the event. What should the planner do first?
choices: Accept the truck and ask for the permit later
Verify the permit's dates and require a current permit before approving the truck to operate
Assume the permit renewed automatically
Charge the truck a fee and let it operate
questions.explain: Operating without a valid permit creates legal and health exposure for the host, so verification comes first.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a risk assessment in event planning?
choices: To set the ticket price
To assign seating
To identify hazards, rate their likelihood and impact, and plan controls
To record guest reviews
questions.explain: A risk assessment ranks hazards so the most serious ones get the most planning effort.

questions.q: Which insurance covers a claim that a guest was injured at an event because of the organizer's negligence?
choices: Auto insurance
Workers' compensation for event staff only
Business interruption insurance
General liability insurance
questions.explain: General liability covers third-party bodily injury and property damage claims arising from the organizer's operations.

questions.q: What is an incident report used for?
choices: Documenting injuries, property damage or unsafe conditions for follow-up and claims
Ranking vendors
Scheduling speakers
Setting the next year's budget
questions.explain: Prompt, factual incident reports support insurance claims and prevent repeat hazards.

questions.q: The fire marshal sets the room's occupancy at 400, but the chapter sells 450 tickets. What is the correct response?
choices: Sell all 450, since the tickets are paid
Cap ticket sales at the lawful occupancy limit and manage the overflow
Ask guests to stand
Remove the fire exits to create space
questions.explain: Exceeding occupancy is a life-safety violation; the lawful limit governs sales.

questions.q: A chapter hires a DJ who is paid in cash under no contract, and the DJ is later injured on site. Which risk is most significant?
choices: Loss of a tax deduction
Marketing confusion
Unclear liability and workers' compensation exposure
Copyright on the music played
questions.explain: Without a contract or proper classification, responsibility for an injury is disputed and costly.

questions.q: What is the first priority in an emergency at an event?
choices: Protect the sponsors' logos
Count the cash
Finish the program
Protect life and safety by following the emergency plan and calling 911 when needed
questions.explain: Life safety comes first; the emergency plan defines who calls for help and who directs guests.

questions.q: Which license allows copyrighted music to be played at a public event?
choices: A public performance license from a performing rights organization such as ASCAP, BMI or SESAC
A driver's license
A sales tax exemption
A trademark registration
questions.explain: Public performance of copyrighted music requires permission, typically through a performing rights organization.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a waiver or release form for event participants?
choices: To guarantee attendance
To document the participant's acknowledgment of known risks and agreement to terms, which may limit claims
To set ticket prices
To replace liability insurance entirely
questions.explain: A waiver can limit some claims, but it does not replace insurance and may not bar every claim.

questions.q: Which action best protects a chapter from volunteer injury claims?
choices: Have volunteers sign no documents
Assume volunteers are never covered
Confirm volunteer accident or liability coverage and provide safety training before setup
Hire volunteers so insurance is not needed
questions.explain: Coverage and training reduce both the risk and the chapter's exposure if an injury occurs.

questions.q: A severe storm warning is issued two hours before an outdoor event. Which action is most appropriate?
choices: Hold the event as planned
Tell guests to bring umbrellas only
Let each vendor decide individually
Follow the pre-set weather decision plan, notify guests and vendors, and move to backup or postpone
questions.explain: A pre-agreed trigger and communication plan avoids panic decisions in the final hours.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a volunteer job description?
choices: To define duties, time commitment and expectations so volunteers know their roles
To set the venue rental price
To record guest feedback
To track sponsor payments
questions.explain: Clear role descriptions reduce confusion and make accountability possible.

questions.q: Three committee chairs are not communicating. Which leadership approach is best?
choices: Let them compete for the lead role
Set a regular check-in schedule, a shared timeline and clear decision authority for each area
Remove one chair from the team
Take over every task personally
questions.explain: Structure and clear authority fix coordination failures without removing people or creating a bottleneck.

questions.q: What is a shift schedule used for during an event?
choices: Recording vendor invoices
Setting the program theme
Assigning staff to times and locations so coverage is clear
Tracking marketing impressions
questions.explain: Shift schedules guarantee coverage at every station and make absences visible quickly.

questions.q: Which method is best for training event staff quickly?
choices: Hand out a manual with no walkthrough
Tell staff to figure it out during the event
Train only the manager
Run a short briefing with a run-of-show walkthrough, role cards and a practice session
questions.explain: A walkthrough and practice build familiarity fast, and role cards keep staff focused on their own tasks.

questions.q: Under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA), which situation most likely requires overtime pay for a paid staff member?
choices: Working 45 hours in a week at a non-exempt hourly rate
Working 45 hours as a volunteer
Working 45 hours as an unpaid nonprofit volunteer
Working 45 hours as an independent contractor
questions.explain: Non-exempt employees must receive time-and-a-half for hours over 40 in a workweek; volunteers and contractors are treated differently.

questions.q: Which statement about nonprofit volunteers is most accurate?
choices: Volunteers must be paid minimum wage
Volunteers generally receive no wages but still need safety training and clear role expectations
Volunteers cannot be given any training
Volunteers must be employees
questions.explain: Volunteer status does not remove the duty to keep volunteers safe and informed.

questions.q: What does a volunteer sign-in sheet support?
choices: Vendor pricing
Ticket sales
Attendance tracking, accountability and emergency headcount
Sponsor recognition only
questions.explain: Sign-in records support accountability and a reliable headcount if an evacuation is needed.

questions.q: A staff member with a personal stake in one caterer is assigned to choose the caterer. What is the best action?
choices: Hide the conflict
Let the staff member choose anyway
Remove all vendors from the process
Disclose the conflict and have another person make the vendor decision
questions.explain: A conflict of interest must be disclosed and managed by reassigning the decision.

questions.q: Which leadership style fits a new volunteer team that needs clear direction?
choices: Directive leadership with clear instructions and frequent check-ins, shifting to supportive leadership as skills grow
Laissez-faire with no check-ins
Delegating all decisions to the newest member
Consensus voting on every task
questions.explain: Teams that are new need direction first; autonomy is earned as competence develops.

questions.q: A volunteer is consistently late for shifts. Which response is most constructive?
choices: Remove the volunteer immediately without discussion
Talk privately, restate expectations, and document the issue and the agreed plan
Ignore it because volunteers are unpaid
Raise the issue publicly with the group
questions.explain: A private, documented conversation addresses the problem fairly and creates a record if the issue continues.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a post-event debrief?
choices: To pay all vendors
To market the next event
To review results against goals, document lessons and recommend changes
To collect sponsor logos
questions.explain: A debrief turns one event's experience into improvements for the next.

questions.q: A chapter's goal was 200 attendees and 180 attended. What is the attainment rate?
choices: 80 percent
110 percent
95 percent
90 percent
questions.explain: Attainment is actual divided by goal: 180 divided by 200 is 0.90, or 90 percent.

questions.q: How is cost per attendee calculated?
choices: Total event cost divided by the number of attendees
Total revenue divided by the number of sponsors
Ticket price multiplied by the number of attendees
Venue capacity divided by the number of attendees
questions.explain: Cost per attendee shows the efficiency of spending and is useful for comparing events.

questions.q: Which metric best evaluates whether a change to the registration process succeeded?
choices: Number of event shirts sold
Completion rate of registrations and the time from starting a registration to a confirmed ticket
Number of social media followers
Size of the venue
questions.explain: Process changes should be judged on the process outcome, such as completion rate and time to confirm.

questions.q: What is a post-mortem in event management?
choices: A pre-event sales pitch
A venue inspection
A structured review of what went well and what to improve after the event
A vendor's final invoice
questions.explain: A post-mortem focuses on learning, not blame, and feeds the next planning cycle.

questions.q: Which data point best evaluates the financial result of a fundraising event?
choices: Number of photos taken
Number of social media posts
Number of programs printed
Net proceeds after all costs, compared to the budget
questions.explain: Net proceeds after costs are the financial result; gross receipts alone overstate the success.

questions.q: Which approach gives a fair picture of attendee satisfaction?
choices: Send a short survey to all attendees and track the response rate
Survey only the VIP guests
Survey only people who complained
Survey only the sponsors
questions.explain: A representative, well-reported survey avoids biased samples, and the response rate shows how far the results can be trusted.

questions.q: A survey of 60 responses shows 70 percent rated the venue good or better, but only 60 of 200 attendees responded. What is the most important caution?
choices: 70 percent is always representative
The response rate is 30 percent, so the results may not represent all attendees
The survey should be discarded entirely
The venue should be rated by staff only
questions.explain: Only 30 percent responded, so non-responders may differ; the result is informative but not conclusive.

questions.q: How should lessons learned from a debrief be used?
choices: Filed without reading
Deleted after one month
Built into planning templates, timelines and vendor checklists for the next event
Shared only with sponsors
questions.explain: Lessons only matter when they change the templates and checklists the team actually uses.

questions.q: Projected net income was $4,000 ($13,000 revenue minus $9,000 expenses). Actual revenue was $12,000 and actual expenses were $10,000. What is the variance on net income?
choices: $2,000 favorable
$1,000 unfavorable
$6,000 favorable
$2,000 unfavorable
questions.explain: Actual net income is $2,000 against a $4,000 budget, a $2,000 unfavorable variance.

vocab.def: A minute-by-minute timeline of every activity, speaker, cue and staff assignment on event day.
A scheduling method that links dependent tasks to find the longest sequence that sets the minimum project duration.
The time between the decision to act and the date the action must be complete, such as booking a vendor before an event.
A pre-set alternative course of action to use if a planned element fails or a risk occurs.
The period when equipment, decor and vendors are brought into the venue before guests arrive.
A goal that is specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound.
The maximum number of people a room may legally hold, set by the local fire authority.
A scaled drawing showing where seating, stages, service areas and exits are placed in a venue.
A room layout with rows of chairs facing the front, used for presentations without dining.
A layout of round tables with chairs for guests to dine together.
A tentative reservation of a date and space that the venue keeps for a limited time before the client must sign.
A pre-event visit to confirm that the space, power, access and exits match the event plan.
A cost that stays the same regardless of attendance or sales volume, such as a venue rental fee.
A cost that changes with the number of guests or units, such as per-plate food cost.
The volume of attendance or sales at which total revenue equals total costs.
The difference between budgeted and actual amounts, labeled favorable or unfavorable.
Money set aside within a budget for unexpected costs.
A non-cash gift of goods or services, recorded at fair value.
A contract clause that excuses performance when extraordinary events beyond a party’s control prevent it.
A document issued by an insurer that confirms a vendor’s coverage limits and policy dates.
A partial payment made to secure a vendor’s services, with refund terms set by the contract.
A contract clause in which one party agrees to cover the other party’s losses from specified claims.
A document that asks vendors to submit detailed proposals for defined services so they can be compared.
A written document setting out the scope, price, dates and responsibilities of a vendor engagement.
The specific group an event or message is designed for and most likely to respond to it.
An explicit instruction telling the audience what to do next, such as register or buy a ticket.
The percentage of people who take a desired action, such as registering, out of those who saw the offer or visited the page.
A discounted ticket price offered for a limited period to encourage early commitment.
The number of times a piece of content is displayed, whether or not it is clicked or read.
A defined set of benefits, such as logo placement and mentions, offered to a sponsor for a set fee.
Any point at which a guest interacts with the event, such as registration, signage or a follow-up email.
The actions taken to restore a guest’s satisfaction after a service failure.
The overall impression a guest forms from every interaction before, during and after an event.
Design and service practices that let people with disabilities use facilities and attend events, required under the Americans with Disabilities Act for public accommodations.
A loyalty measure based on how likely guests are to recommend an experience, on a scale of 0 to 10.
A staff function that helps guests with requests, information and problems during an event or stay.
A stock rotation method in which the oldest inventory is used or sold first.
The temperature range of about 40 to 140 degrees F (4 to 60 degrees C) in which bacteria multiply rapidly.
Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Points, a systematic food-safety method that identifies and controls hazards at critical points.
A guest or place setting charged for a meal, used as a unit of banquet pricing.
Food cost divided by menu price, expressed as a percentage, used to judge menu pricing.
A tested recipe with fixed ingredients, portions and method that allows consistent quality and cost per serving.
A process that identifies hazards, rates their likelihood and impact, and plans controls for each.
Coverage that pays for third-party bodily injury and property damage claims arising from the insured’s operations.
A signed document in which a participant acknowledges known risks and agrees to terms that may limit claims.
A written record of an injury, damage or unsafe condition, used for follow-up and insurance claims.
Permission to publicly play copyrighted music, typically obtained through an organization such as ASCAP, BMI or SESAC.
Failure to exercise the care a reasonable person would in the same situation, which can create liability when it causes harm.
A written statement of a role’s duties, responsibilities, time commitment and expectations.
A plan that assigns staff or volunteers to specific times and locations so coverage is clear.
Pay at one and one-half times the regular rate for hours worked over 40 in a workweek by non-exempt employees.
Under the FLSA, an exempt employee is not eligible for overtime pay, and a non-exempt employee is eligible for it.
A situation in which a personal interest could improperly influence a professional decision, requiring disclosure and recusal.
A leadership style that gives clear instructions and close oversight, suited to new or inexperienced teams.
A structured meeting after an event to review results against goals and capture lessons learned.
Actual results divided by the goal, expressed as a percentage.
Total event cost divided by the number of attendees, used to measure spending efficiency.
The amount left after all costs are subtracted from gross revenue.
The number of survey responses divided by the number of people invited, used to judge how representative results are.
A review of the differences between budgeted and actual results to explain why they occurred.
